Case: Make the Road New York v. Huffman
D.C. Circuit allows expansion of expedited removal
D.C. Circuit rejects challenge to expedited removal policy; is an en banc petition to follow?

status_summary: A DHS notice signed by Acting Secretary Benjamine Huffman, filed and effective on 2025-01-21 and published 2025-01-24 (90 FR 8139), extends expedited removal to people who did not arrive by sea and cannot show two years of continuous presence, whether apprehended anywhere in the interior or within 100 air miles of a land border (where the earlier 14-day limit is replaced), and rescinds the 2022 notice that had limited it. A district court stayed the notice on 2025-08-29 in Make the Road New York v. Noem; the D.C. Circuit left that stay largely in place in November 2025 and March 2026. On 2026-06-23 a divided D.C. Circuit panel vacated the stay, and per AILA the court on 2026-07-17 allowed the expansion to take effect immediately. Plaintiffs filed a petition for rehearing en banc on 2026-07-27, arguing the due process holding conflicts with a Supreme Court decision and asking at minimum for a remand so the district court can review procedures the government newly disclosed. No ruling on the petition and no Supreme Court filing were found.

timeline.event: DHS notice designating aliens for expedited removal takes effect (filed for public inspection 2025-01-21; published 2025-01-24 at 90 FR 8139), rescinding the 2022 limit and covering interior arrests of people present under two years.
Make the Road New York sues in D.D.C. (Judge Jia Cobb).
Judge Cobb stays the designation and the Huffman memorandum under APA section 705, finding plaintiffs likely to succeed on a due process claim.
D.C. Circuit denies the government's stay request as to the expansion order and memorandum, granting it only as to certain credible-fear and removal-procedure changes.
D.C. Circuit denies the government's renewed emergency stay motion.

D.C. Circuit (Walker, Rao, Wilkins; 2 to 1 on the merits) vacates the district court stay, holding the designation likely does not violate due process; Judge Rao would have found no jurisdiction; Judge Wilkins dissented in part.
timeline.source: U.S. Court of Appeals for the D.C. Circuit

timeline.event: D.C. Circuit grants the government's renewed motion so the expansion takes effect before the mandate issues (per AILA).
